name: Dustin Moskovitz
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Facebook and led early engineering/operations
starting_point: Born in Gainesville, Florida and raised in Ocala, Florida; attended an IB program at Vanguard High School before enrolling at Harvard to study economics.
current_position: Chairman of the board of Asana; stepped down as CEO in July 2025; net worth estimated at ~$10.2 billion as of 2025.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Facebook
trajectory.description: Co-founded Facebook with Mark Zuckerberg and roommates at Harvard in February 2004, serving as the company's first CTO and later VP of Engineering.

trajectory.title: Moved to Palo Alto
trajectory.description: Took a leave from Harvard in June 2004 and moved to Palo Alto with Zuckerberg to work on Facebook full-time.

trajectory.title: Left Facebook to start Asana
trajectory.description: Departed Facebook in October 2008 to co-found Asana with Justin Rosenstein, aiming to improve workplace productivity and project management.

trajectory.title: Youngest self-made billionaire
trajectory.description: Forbes named Moskovitz the world's youngest self-made billionaire in March 2011 based on his Facebook shares.

trajectory.title: Asana launched publicly
trajectory.description: Asana's product launched to the public, offering team-based project and task management for enterprises.

trajectory.title: Asana IPO
trajectory.description: Asana went public on the NYSE via a direct listing, valuing the company at over $5 billion.

trajectory.title: Stepped down as Asana CEO
trajectory.description: Retired as Asana CEO in July 2025 after 15 years, transitioning to chairman of the board.

name: Eduardo Saverin
starting_point: Born in São Paulo to a wealthy Jewish-Brazilian family; father was a businessman in clothing, shipping, energy, and real estate; family emigrated to Miami, Florida in 1993.
current_position: Co-founder and co-CEO of B Capital Group, a venture capital firm with over $7 billion AUM; resident of Singapore; net worth estimated at ~$30 billion as of 2025.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Facebook
trajectory.description: Co-founded Facebook with Mark Zuckerberg at Harvard, providing initial funding of ~$15,000 and serving as CFO and business manager.

trajectory.title: Ousted from Facebook
trajectory.description: Forced out of Facebook management in summer 2004 after disputes with Zuckerberg over company direction and equity.

trajectory.title: Sued Zuckerberg
trajectory.description: Filed lawsuits against Zuckerberg and Facebook over diluted shares; eventually reached a settlement that restored a small stake.

trajectory.title: Graduated from Harvard
trajectory.description: Graduated magna cum laude from Harvard with a BA in economics.

trajectory.title: Moved to Singapore
trajectory.description: Relocated to Singapore, beginning a new chapter as an angel investor in Southeast Asian tech startups.

trajectory.title: Renounced US citizenship
trajectory.description: Renounced his US citizenship ahead of Facebook's IPO, a move widely reported as tax-motivated; retained his ~2% stake in Facebook.

trajectory.title: Co-founded B Capital
trajectory.description: Launched venture capital firm B Capital with Raj Ganguly, growing it to over $7 billion in assets under management.

trajectory.title: Singapore's richest person
trajectory.description: Named Singapore's richest person by Forbes with an estimated net worth of ~$30 billion, largely from Meta shares and B Capital.

name: Sean Parker
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Napster and later became a key early Facebook operator
starting_point: Born in Herndon, Virginia; father was a US government oceanographer and chief scientist at NOAA, mother was a TV advertising broker; father taught him programming on an Atari 800 at age seven.
current_position: Founder and chairman of the Parker Foundation, focused on life sciences, global public health, and civic engagement; net worth estimated at ~$3 billion as of 2025.

trajectory.title: Early hacking and FBI encounter
trajectory.description: Caught by the FBI at age 16 for hacking into Fortune 500 company networks; sentenced to community service.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Napster
trajectory.description: Co-founded Napster with Shawn Fanning, the peer-to-peer file-sharing service that attracted tens of millions of users and upended the music industry.

trajectory.title: Napster shut down
trajectory.description: Napster was ordered to shut down by court order after copyright infringement lawsuits from the RIAA; Parker was forced out earlier.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Plaxo
trajectory.description: Co-founded Plaxo, an online address book and social networking service that pioneered viral growth mechanics; was later removed from the company in 2004.

trajectory.title: Became Facebook's first president
trajectory.description: Joined the five-month-old Facebook as its founding president, brought on Peter Thiel as first outside investor, and helped Zuckerberg retain control.

trajectory.title: Left Facebook presidency
trajectory.description: Forced out of Facebook after a drug-related arrest, though he remained an advisor and retained equity.

trajectory.title: Spotify investment
trajectory.description: Led a $15 million investment in Spotify at a $5 million valuation, helping bring the music service to the US.

trajectory.title: Launched the Parker Foundation
trajectory.description: Founded the Parker Foundation with a $600 million initial commitment, focusing on life sciences and global public health.

name: Shawn Fanning
starting_point: Born in Brockton, Massachusetts; worked summers at his uncle's Internet company Chess.net; attended Northeastern University briefly before dropping out.
current_position: Angel investor and entrepreneur; founder of Helium and previously Path; based in San Francisco.

trajectory.title: Dropped out of Northeastern
trajectory.description: Left Northeastern University after one semester to focus full-time on writing the Napster code at his uncle's office in Hull, Massachusetts.

trajectory.title: Launched Napster
trajectory.description: Launched Napster in June 1999, the peer-to-peer file-sharing service that revolutionized how people discovered and shared music online.

trajectory.title: Time magazine cover
trajectory.description: Featured on the cover of Time magazine, becoming the face of the digital music revolution while still a teenager.

trajectory.title: Napster shut down
trajectory.description: Napster was shut down by court order in July 2001 after losing copyright infringement lawsuits from the recording industry.

trajectory.title: Founded SNOCAP
trajectory.description: Co-founded SNOCAP, a digital rights management and licensing startup that aimed to create a legitimate digital music marketplace.

trajectory.title: Founded Rupture
trajectory.description: Founded Rupture, a social network for online gamers, which was later acquired by Electronic Arts in 2008.

trajectory.title: Founded Path
trajectory.description: Co-founded Path, a private social networking app, which launched in November 2010 and grew to over 10 million users.

trajectory.title: Founded Helium
trajectory.description: Founded Helium, a decentralized wireless network startup, continuing his pattern of building category-defining internet products.

name: Jerry Yang
milestone_by_age_26: Co-created Yahoo as an early web directory
starting_point: Born in Taipei, Taiwan; father died when he was two; mother moved the family to San Jose, California in 1978 where she taught English to immigrants; knew only the word 'shoe' in English upon arrival.
current_position: Founding partner of AME Cloud Ventures; chair of the Stanford Board of Trustees; net worth estimated at ~$2.6 billion as of 2025.

trajectory.title: Graduated from Stanford
trajectory.description: Earned both BS and MS in electrical engineering from Stanford University in four years, where he met future co-founder David Filo.

trajectory.title: Co-created Yahoo directory
trajectory.description: Co-created 'Jerry and David's Guide to the World Wide Web' with David Filo while PhD students at Stanford, a directory of websites that became Yahoo!.

trajectory.title: Founded Yahoo! Inc.
trajectory.description: Incorporated Yahoo! with venture capital funding from Sequoia Capital, dropping out of the Stanford PhD program.

trajectory.title: Yahoo IPO
trajectory.description: Yahoo went public in April 1996, with shares surging on the first day of trading and establishing Yahoo as a leading internet company.

trajectory.title: Alibaba investment
trajectory.description: Led Yahoo's $1 billion investment in Alibaba for a 40% stake, widely considered one of the most lucrative deals in Silicon Valley history.

trajectory.title: Became Yahoo CEO
trajectory.description: Returned as CEO of Yahoo in June 2007, serving until January 2009 during a turbulent period for the company.

trajectory.title: Left Yahoo board
trajectory.description: Resigned from Yahoo's board of directors in January 2012, ending his formal association with the company he co-founded.

trajectory.title: Founded AME Cloud Ventures
trajectory.description: Established AME Cloud Ventures, a venture capital firm focused on data-driven startups, reinventing himself as a mentor and investor.

name: Max Levchin
starting_point: Born in Kyiv, Ukrainian SSR to a Ukrainian-Jewish family; emigrated to Chicago in 1991 as a refugee with his family, arriving with $700; had severe respiratory problems as a child.
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of Affirm Holdings; net worth estimated at ~$1.2 billion as of 2025; resides in San Francisco.

trajectory.title: Graduated from University of Illinois
trajectory.description: Earned a BS in computer science from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, having founded four startups during his studies.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Confinity/PayPal
trajectory.description: Co-founded Fieldlink (later Confinity, then PayPal) with Peter Thiel, building a digital wallet for PalmPilots that evolved into the PayPal payment service.

trajectory.title: Created CAPTCHA technology
trajectory.description: Co-created the Gausebeck-Levchin test, one of the first commercial CAPTCHA implementations, as part of PayPal's anti-fraud efforts.

trajectory.title: PayPal acquired by eBay
trajectory.description: PayPal was acquired by eBay for $1.5 billion; Levchin served as CTO through the IPO and acquisition.

trajectory.title: Founded Slide
trajectory.description: Founded Slide, a social networking and photo-sharing application company that reached over 150 million monthly users at its peak.

trajectory.title: Slide acquired by Google
trajectory.description: Slide was acquired by Google for ~$182 million; Levchin joined Google as VP of Engineering but left within a year.

trajectory.title: Founded Affirm
trajectory.description: Founded Affirm, a buy-now-pay-later fintech lending company, launching the service publicly in 2014.

trajectory.title: Affirm IPO
trajectory.description: Affirm went public on NASDAQ in January 2021, with shares surging over 100% on the first day, valuing the company at over $12 billion.

name: Tony Hsieh
starting_point: Born in Urbana, Illinois to Taiwanese immigrant parents; graduated from Harvard with a degree in computer science; worked briefly at Oracle before leaving to start LinkExchange.
current_position: Died on November 27, 2020 at age 46 from injuries sustained in a house fire in Bridgeport, Connecticut; final role: retired CEO of Zappos (stepped down August 2020).

trajectory.title: Graduated from Harvard
trajectory.description: Graduated from Harvard with a degree in computer science; worked at Oracle Corporation for five months before leaving to pursue entrepreneurship.

trajectory.title: Co-founded LinkExchange
trajectory.description: Co-founded LinkExchange, an internet advertising network, with Sanjay Madan and Ali Partovi; grew to 400,000+ members within two years.

trajectory.title: Sold LinkExchange to Microsoft
trajectory.description: Sold LinkExchange to Microsoft for $265 million, personally netting $40 million; then co-founded Venture Frogs, an investment incubator.

trajectory.title: Joined Zappos
trajectory.description: Joined Zappos (initially ShoeSite.com) as an investor and advisor, eventually becoming CEO and building it into a billion-dollar online shoe retailer.

trajectory.title: Zappos acquired by Amazon
trajectory.description: Amazon acquired Zappos for ~$1.2 billion in a stock-and-cash deal; Hsieh remained as CEO.

trajectory.title: Published Delivering Happiness
trajectory.description: Published the bestselling memoir 'Delivering Happiness: A Path to Profits, Passion, and Purpose,' chronicling his entrepreneurial journey and company culture philosophy.

trajectory.title: Launched Downtown Project
trajectory.description: Invested $350 million of his own money into revitalizing downtown Las Vegas through the Downtown Project, aiming to create a vibrant urban tech hub.

trajectory.title: Died in house fire
trajectory.description: Died on November 27, 2020 from complications of a fire at a residence in Bridgeport, Connecticut, after retiring as Zappos CEO in August 2020.

name: Garrett Camp
starting_point: Born and raised in Calgary, Alberta, Canada; father was an economist and contractor, mother an artist and designer; fell in love with computers at age 10 when his uncle lent him a Macintosh Plus.
current_position: Founder of Expa, a startup incubator; co-founder and board member of Uber; net worth estimated at ~$6.2 billion as of 2025; resides in Los Angeles.

trajectory.title: Co-founded StumbleUpon
trajectory.description: Co-founded StumbleUpon while in graduate school at the University of Calgary, creating the first personalized content discovery engine.

trajectory.title: Moved StumbleUpon to San Francisco
trajectory.description: Relocated StumbleUpon to the San Francisco Bay Area after securing $1.2 million in angel funding.

trajectory.title: StumbleUpon acquired by eBay
trajectory.description: StumbleUpon was acquired by eBay for $75 million; Camp continued to run the company but grew frustrated with corporate constraints.

trajectory.title: Spun out StumbleUpon and co-founded Uber
trajectory.description: Bought StumbleUpon back from eBay in 2009; also co-founded Uber (originally UberCab) with Travis Kalanick the same year.

trajectory.title: Stepped down as StumbleUpon CEO
trajectory.description: Stepped down as CEO of StumbleUpon to focus on Uber and other ventures; remained as chairman.

trajectory.title: Founded Expa
trajectory.description: Founded Expa, a startup incubator designed to help founders build new companies from scratch.

trajectory.title: StumbleUpon shut down
trajectory.description: Shut down StumbleUpon and transitioned it to Mix, a successor product built through Expa Labs.

trajectory.title: Left Uber board
trajectory.description: Left Uber's board of directors but remained as a board observer, having been a co-founder since 2009.

name: Aaron Levie
starting_point: Born in Boulder, Colorado; family moved to Mercer Island, Washington when he was ten; father was a chemical engineer at a paper company, mother a speech-language pathologist; attended University of Southern California.
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of Box, Inc.; the company serves over 170,000 enterprise customers; resides in the San Francisco Bay Area.

trajectory.title: Conceived Box as college project
trajectory.description: Developed the idea for Box as a college business project at USC, identifying a fragmented market for enterprise cloud storage.

trajectory.title: Launched Box with Mark Cuban investment
trajectory.description: Cold-emailed Mark Cuban, who invested $300,000; took a leave of absence from USC to launch Box (originally box.net) with co-founder Dylan Smith.

trajectory.title: Pivoted to enterprise focus
trajectory.description: Pivoted Box from consumer cloud storage to enterprise content management, targeting Fortune 500 companies.

trajectory.title: Raised major funding rounds
trajectory.description: Box raised over $150 million in venture funding, valuing the company at over $1 billion and establishing it as a leader in enterprise cloud content management.

trajectory.title: Box IPO
trajectory.description: Box went public on the NYSE in January 2015, raising $175 million and valuing the company at ~$2.7 billion.

trajectory.title: Stepped down as board chair
trajectory.description: Transitioned from chairman of the board to focus on CEO role, continuing to lead Box's evolution as a content cloud platform.

name: Dylan Smith
starting_point: Attended Duke University; met Aaron Levie through mutual connections and became his co-founder at Box while still a student.
current_position: Co-founder and former CFO of Box, Inc.; transitioned from CFO role in 2017; remains on the board.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Box
trajectory.description: Co-founded Box (originally box.net) with Aaron Levie, serving as CFO while still attending Duke University.

trajectory.title: Secured Mark Cuban investment
trajectory.description: Helped secure a $300,000 angel investment from Mark Cuban after Levie's cold email pitch, enabling the company to launch.

trajectory.title: Became full-time CFO
trajectory.description: Officially served as CFO of Box from February 2009, managing the company's finances through rapid growth and multiple funding rounds.

trajectory.title: Box IPO
trajectory.description: Box went public on the NYSE in January 2015, with Smith having overseen the company's financial operations through the IPO.

trajectory.title: Stepped down as CFO
trajectory.description: Transitioned from the CFO role in January 2017, having served in that capacity for eight years through the company's growth and public offering.

name: Arash Ferdowsi
starting_point: Born in Overland Park, Kansas to Iranian immigrant parents; graduated first in his class from Blue Valley Northwest High School; attended MIT for electrical engineering and computer science.
current_position: Co-founder of Dropbox; left Dropbox in 2020; net worth estimated at over $1 billion; angel investor and advisor.

trajectory.title: Google internship
trajectory.description: Completed a software engineering internship at Google in Kirkland, Washington during the summer before his senior year at MIT.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Dropbox
trajectory.description: Co-founded Dropbox with Drew Houston in June 2007, dropping out of MIT in his last semester to build the company in San Francisco.

trajectory.title: Raised seed funding from Y Combinator
trajectory.description: Dropbox joined Y Combinator and raised $1.2 million from Sequoia Capital, Accel, and other investors.

trajectory.title: Launched Dropbox publicly
trajectory.description: Dropbox launched to the public, offering seamless cloud file synchronization that quickly attracted millions of users.

trajectory.title: Stepped down as CTO
trajectory.description: Transitioned from CTO role in October 2016 after nine years, remaining on the board of directors.

trajectory.title: Dropbox IPO
trajectory.description: Dropbox went public on NASDAQ in March 2018, valuing the company at ~$9.2 billion.

trajectory.title: Left Dropbox board
trajectory.description: Departed Dropbox's board of directors in March 2020, ending his formal association with the company he co-founded.

name: Nathan Blecharczyk
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Airbnb as technical co-founder and built the platform
starting_point: Born in 1983 in Boston, Massachusetts to an upper-middle-class family; father was Polish American; attended Boston Latin Academy; made money in high school through a web-hosting business that earned over $1 million.
current_position: Co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer of Airbnb; chairman of Airbnb China; net worth estimated at ~$9.4 billion as of 2025; resides in San Francisco.

trajectory.title: Ran profitable web-hosting business
trajectory.description: Operated a self-taught web-hosting business from high school that earned over $1 million, though it was once listed on the Spamhaus Project's registry of known spam operators.

trajectory.title: Graduated from Harvard
trajectory.description: Graduated from Harvard with a BS in computer science, having shut down his web-hosting business to focus on studies.

trajectory.title: Worked as lead developer at Batiq
trajectory.description: Worked as a lead developer at Batiq before connecting with Joe Gebbia, who was looking for a roommate in San Francisco.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Airbnb
trajectory.description: Co-founded Airbnb with Brian Chesky and Joe Gebbia, coding the original website in Ruby on Rails and serving as the company's first CTO.

trajectory.title: Joined Y Combinator
trajectory.description: Airbnb joined Y Combinator's winter 2009 batch, receiving $20,000 in seed funding that helped the company survive near-collapse.

trajectory.title: Transitioned to Chief Strategy Officer
trajectory.description: Moved from CTO to Chief Strategy Officer role, focusing on global strategic initiatives and government relations.

trajectory.title: Airbnb IPO
trajectory.description: Airbnb went public on NASDAQ in December 2020, with shares doubling on the first day and valuing the company at over $100 billion.

trajectory.title: Chairman of Airbnb China
trajectory.description: Serves as chairman of Airbnb China and continues as CSO, overseeing strategic initiatives and the Airbnb City Portal.

name: David Karp
starting_point: Born in New York City, grew up on the Upper West Side of Manhattan; father was a film and television composer, mother a science teacher at the Calhoun School; taught himself HTML at age 11 and dropped out of high school at 15.
current_position: Left Tumblr in 2017; angel investor and entrepreneur; founded a new startup called Inventory; resides in New York City.

trajectory.title: Became CTO of UrbanBaby
trajectory.description: Dropped out of high school at 15 and became head of technology at UrbanBaby, a New York City parenting website, without a high school diploma.

trajectory.title: Started software consulting company
trajectory.description: Founded Davidville, a software consulting company, where he worked with engineer Marco Arment on client projects.

trajectory.title: Launched Tumblr
trajectory.description: Launched Tumblr in February 2007 during a gap between consulting contracts; the microblogging platform gained 75,000 users within two weeks.

trajectory.title: Named Best Young Tech Entrepreneur
trajectory.description: Named Best Young Tech Entrepreneur 2009 by BusinessWeek as Tumblr grew to host millions of blogs.

trajectory.title: MIT TR35 recognition
trajectory.description: Named to the MIT Technology Review TR35 list of top 35 innovators under 35 worldwide.

trajectory.title: Yahoo acquired Tumblr for $1.1 billion
trajectory.description: Yahoo acquired Tumblr for $1.1 billion; Karp remained as CEO with an $81 million retention package.

trajectory.title: Left Tumblr
trajectory.description: Announced departure from Tumblr in November 2017, after the platform hosted over 375 million blogs at its peak.

name: Matt Mullenweg
starting_point: Born and raised in Houston, Texas; father was a computer programmer; attended the High School for the Performing and Visual Arts; studied at the University of Houston before dropping out in 2004.
current_position: CEO of Automattic and co-founder of WordPress; WordPress powers over 43% of all websites; resides in San Francisco.

trajectory.title: Co-created WordPress
trajectory.description: Co-created WordPress with Mike Little in January 2003 as a fork of the b2/cafelog blogging platform, while a student at the University of Houston.

trajectory.title: Dropped out of college
trajectory.description: Left the University of Houston to work full-time on WordPress and related projects.

trajectory.title: Founded Automattic
trajectory.description: Founded Automattic, the company behind WordPress.com, Jetpack, WooCommerce, and other web products, to commercialize the WordPress ecosystem.

trajectory.title: Worked at CNET
trajectory.description: Worked at CNET Networks in San Francisco before leaving in late 2005 to focus on Automattic full-time.

trajectory.title: Became CEO of Automattic
trajectory.description: Took on the CEO role at Automattic, leading the company through significant growth and funding rounds.

trajectory.title: Automattic raised $300 million
trajectory.description: Automattic raised $300 million in Series D funding, valuing the company at $3 billion.

trajectory.title: Acquired Tumblr from Verizon
trajectory.description: Automattic acquired Tumblr from Verizon for a reported $3 million, bringing the platform under the WordPress ecosystem.

trajectory.title: WordPress 20th anniversary
trajectory.description: Celebrated 20 years of WordPress, which had grown to power over 43% of all websites globally.

name: David Heinemeier Hansson
milestone_by_age_26: Created Ruby on Rails and became a Basecamp partner
starting_point: Born in Copenhagen, Denmark; learned PHP in high school while creating gaming review sites; studied business administration and computer science at Copenhagen Business School.
current_position: Co-owner and CTO of 37signals (Basecamp); creator of Ruby on Rails; resides in Malibu, California; also a competitive racing driver.

trajectory.title: Founded Daily Rush
trajectory.description: Founded and built a Danish online gaming news website and community called Daily Rush, which he ran until 2001.

trajectory.title: Joined 37signals
trajectory.description: Was hired by Jason Fried after impressing him with PHP coding help; began working remotely from Denmark on what became Basecamp.

trajectory.title: Created Ruby on Rails
trajectory.description: Extracted the Ruby on Rails web framework from his Basecamp development work and released it as open source in 2004.

trajectory.title: Named Hacker of the Year
trajectory.description: Received Google and O'Reilly's 'Hacker of the Year' award for creating Ruby on Rails, which would go on to power GitHub, Shopify, Airbnb, and more.

trajectory.title: Immigrated to the US
trajectory.description: Moved to the United States from Denmark after graduating from Copenhagen Business School with a degree in business administration and computer science.

trajectory.title: Published REWORK
trajectory.description: Co-authored REWORK with Jason Fried, a New York Times and Wall Street Journal bestseller about building businesses differently.

trajectory.title: Published REMOTE
trajectory.description: Co-authored REMOTE: Office Not Required, advocating for remote work years before it became mainstream.

trajectory.title: Launched HEY
trajectory.description: Launched HEY, a revolutionary email service, through 37signals, challenging the conventions of email with a fresh approach.

name: Austin Russell
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Luminar and later received a Thiel Fellowship
starting_point: Born in Newport Beach, California; parents introduced him to laser entrepreneur Jason Eichenholz at age 15, who became his mentor; studied at the Beckman Laser Institute at UC Irvine while in high school.
current_position: Founder and former CEO of Luminar Technologies, which filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in December 2025; subject of legal proceedings; net worth diminished significantly.

trajectory.title: Founded Luminar
trajectory.description: Founded Luminar Technologies while still in high school, shortly before turning 17, focusing on lidar and machine perception for autonomous vehicles.

trajectory.title: Thiel Fellowship and dropped out of Stanford
trajectory.description: Won a $100,000 Thiel Fellowship and dropped out of Stanford after three months to focus on Luminar full-time.

trajectory.title: Developed breakthrough lidar technology
trajectory.description: Developed lidar sensors capable of detecting objects at 250 meters, a significant breakthrough for autonomous vehicle perception.

trajectory.title: Luminar IPO
trajectory.description: Luminar went public via SPAC in December 2020, temporarily making Russell the world's youngest self-made billionaire.

trajectory.title: Secured major auto partnerships
trajectory.description: Secured partnerships with Volvo, Toyota, and other major automakers to integrate Luminar's lidar technology into production vehicles.

trajectory.title: Attempted Forbes acquisition
trajectory.description: Began negotiating to become majority owner of Forbes; the deal fell through in November 2023 after Russell was unable to fund it.

trajectory.title: Luminar filed for bankruptcy
trajectory.description: Luminar Technologies filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in December 2025; Russell became subject to legal proceedings involving bankruptcy obligations and a defaulted personal loan.

name: Nick D'Aloisio
milestone_by_age_26: Built Summly, later sold to Yahoo
starting_point: Born in Melbourne, Australia; moved to London at age seven with his lawyer mother and banker father; attended King's College School, an independent school in Wimbledon.
current_position: Philosophy PhD student at Oxford University; founder of Sphere (acquired by Twitter in 2021); angel investor and philosopher.

trajectory.title: Built TrimIt app
trajectory.description: Created TrimIt, a news summarization iPhone app, at age 15 while revising for a history exam; secured $300,000 from Li Ka-shing's fund.

trajectory.title: Launched Summly
trajectory.description: Launched Summly, an AI-powered news summarization app, becoming the youngest person to receive venture capital funding in technology at age 16.

trajectory.title: Sold Summly to Yahoo for $30M
trajectory.description: Sold Summly to Yahoo for a reported $30 million at age 17, becoming one of Yahoo's youngest employees.

trajectory.title: Launched Yahoo News Digest
trajectory.description: Launched Yahoo News Digest, which won an Apple Design Award in 2014; began studying philosophy and computer science at Hertford College, Oxford.

trajectory.title: Left Yahoo
trajectory.description: Left Yahoo to focus on studies at Oxford University; did a stint as Entrepreneur in Residence at Airbnb.

trajectory.title: Sphere acquired by Twitter
trajectory.description: Founded Sphere, a knowledge-sharing startup that raised $30M from Index Ventures; acquired by Twitter in October 2021 for an undisclosed sum.

trajectory.title: Began PhD in Philosophy at Oxford
trajectory.description: Advanced to the DPhil (PhD) program in Philosophy at Oxford University, having completed the BPhil in 2021, with multiple peer-reviewed papers accepted.

name: Josh Browder
starting_point: Born in 1997 in London, England; grew up in London before moving to Palo Alto at age 18; has dyslexia and dyspraxia; taught himself to code from YouTube videos at age 12; father attended Stanford.
current_position: Founder and CEO of DoNotPay, the world's first AI legal services company; solo GP at Browder Capital; resides in the San Francisco Bay Area.

trajectory.title: Built DoNotPay
trajectory.description: Coded the first version of DoNotPay in a single night to help people contest parking tickets, launching it as a free chatbot that went viral on Reddit.

trajectory.title: Enrolled at Stanford
trajectory.description: Enrolled at Stanford University to study computer science, continuing to build DoNotPay while a student.

trajectory.title: Awarded Thiel Fellowship
trajectory.description: Received a Thiel Fellowship, dropping out of Stanford to focus on DoNotPay full-time.

trajectory.title: Expanded DoNotPay to 200+ services
trajectory.description: Expanded DoNotPay from parking tickets to over 200 consumer rights processes, including canceling subscriptions, lowering bills, and obtaining refunds.

trajectory.title: Raised $12M Series A
trajectory.description: Raised $12 million in Series A funding at an $80 million valuation from Coatue, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, and Felicis Ventures.

trajectory.title: Named MIT TR35 innovator
trajectory.description: Named one of MIT Technology Review's 35 Innovators Under 35 for pioneering AI-powered legal services.

trajectory.title: Launched Browder Capital
trajectory.description: Became a solo GP at Browder Capital, a venture fund investing in first-time entrepreneurs, having personally invested in over 150 companies including Figma and Mercury.

name: Boyan Slat
starting_point: Born on July 27, 1994 in Delft, Netherlands; went scuba diving in Greece at age 16 and saw more plastic bags than fish, which inspired his life's mission.
current_position: Founder and CEO of The Ocean Cleanup, a non-profit developing technologies to rid the world's oceans of plastic; based in the Netherlands.

trajectory.title: Ocean plastic school project
trajectory.description: Made ocean plastic pollution the subject of a high school science project after a diving trip in Greece, developing the idea for a passive catchment system.

trajectory.title: TEDx talk went viral
trajectory.description: Presented his ocean cleanup idea at a TEDx conference in Delft in late 2012; the video went viral in February 2013 after being shared by news blogs.

trajectory.title: Founded The Ocean Cleanup
trajectory.description: Dropped out of aerospace engineering at TU Delft and founded The Ocean Cleanup with €300 in savings, launching a crowdfunding campaign that raised $2.2 million from 38,000 donors.

trajectory.title: Published feasibility study
trajectory.description: Published a 528-page feasibility study about the ocean cleanup project, establishing scientific credibility despite criticism from some marine scientists.

trajectory.title: Launched System 001
trajectory.description: Launched the first ocean cleanup system, a 2,000-foot floating barrier, from San Francisco into the Great Pacific Garbage Patch.

trajectory.title: Achieved Proof of Technology
trajectory.description: Successfully achieved Proof of Technology for both river interception and Great Pacific Garbage Patch cleanup, validating the approach after years of iteration.

trajectory.title: Scaling operations globally
trajectory.description: The Ocean Cleanup continues scaling its river interception systems and ocean cleanup arrays, with the goal of removing 90% of floating ocean plastic by 2040.

name: George Hotz
milestone_by_age_26: Became known for unlocking the iPhone; founded comma.ai at 25
starting_point: Born on October 2, 1989 in Glen Rock, New Jersey; became known online as 'geohot'; attended Rochester Institute of Technology and Carnegie Mellon but never completed a degree.
current_position: Founder and president of comma.ai; working on tinygrad, a deep learning framework; based in San Diego, California.

trajectory.title: First to unlock the iPhone
trajectory.description: Became the first person reported to remove the SIM lock on the iPhone, trading his unlocked device for a Nissan 350Z and three iPhones.

trajectory.title: Released blackra1n jailbreak
trajectory.description: Released blackra1n, a widely used iOS jailbreak compatible with all iPhone and iPod Touch devices running iOS 3.1.2.

trajectory.title: Reverse-engineered PlayStation 3
trajectory.description: Reverse-engineered the PlayStation 3, leading to a lawsuit from Sony that was settled out of court.

trajectory.title: Worked at Facebook
trajectory.description: Worked at Facebook from May 2011 to January 2012 as part of a brief stint in corporate tech.

trajectory.title: Joined Google Project Zero
trajectory.description: Hired by Google to work with the Project Zero team, where he developed Qira for dynamic binary analysis.

trajectory.title: Founded comma.ai
trajectory.description: Founded comma.ai in September 2015, a vehicle automation and machine learning company aiming to democratize self-driving technology.

trajectory.title: Raised $3.1M from Andreessen Horowitz
trajectory.description: Secured a $3.1 million investment from Andreessen Horowitz for comma.ai, building autonomous driving kits from his garage.

trajectory.title: Started tinygrad
trajectory.description: Began working on tinygrad, a deep learning framework, while continuing to lead comma.ai's openpilot project.

name: Alexandr Wang
starting_point: Born in January 1997 in Los Alamos, New Mexico; son of Chinese immigrant physicists who worked at Los Alamos National Laboratory; qualified for the US Math Olympiad and US Physics Team in high school.
current_position: Chief AI Officer of Meta Platforms and head of Meta Superintelligence Labs; founder of Scale AI; net worth estimated at ~$3.6 billion as of 2025.

trajectory.title: Engineering jobs in Silicon Valley
trajectory.description: Landed full-time engineering jobs at age 17 at Addepar and then Quora, where he met future co-founder Lucy Guo.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Scale AI
trajectory.description: Dropped out of MIT after freshman year to co-found Scale AI with Lucy Guo through Y Combinator's summer 2016 batch.

trajectory.title: Scale AI rapid growth
trajectory.description: Scale AI grew rapidly, providing data labeling services for autonomous vehicle companies and AI labs, raising $100 million at a $1 billion valuation.

trajectory.title: Youngest self-made billionaire
trajectory.description: Became the world's youngest self-made billionaire at age 24 after Scale AI raised $325 million at a $7.3 billion valuation.

trajectory.title: Scale AI valued at $14 billion
trajectory.description: Scale AI raised $1 billion in Series F funding, valuing the company at $14 billion and expanding into AI model evaluation services.

trajectory.title: Joined Meta as Chief AI Officer
trajectory.description: Meta acquired 49% of Scale AI for $14.3 billion; Wang left as CEO to become Meta's Chief AI Officer, leading its new Superintelligence Labs.

name: Lucy Guo
starting_point: Born in 1994 in California, raised in Fremont by Chinese immigrant parents who were both electrical engineers; taught herself to code in elementary school to play Neopets; dropped out of Carnegie Mellon for the Thiel Fellowship.
current_position: Founder and CEO of Passes, a creator platform; youngest self-made female billionaire as of 2025; net worth estimated at ~$1.2 billion; resides in Los Angeles.

trajectory.title: Thiel Fellowship and dropped out
trajectory.description: Dropped out of Carnegie Mellon University after being selected for the Thiel Fellowship, a $100,000 grant for young entrepreneurs.

trajectory.title: Worked at Snapchat and Quora
trajectory.description: Interned at Facebook, then joined Snapchat as its first female designer helping develop Snap Maps, before moving to Quora where she met Alexandr Wang.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Scale AI
trajectory.description: Co-founded Scale AI with Alexandr Wang through Y Combinator, building the first version of the core product in a weekend.

trajectory.title: Fired from Scale AI
trajectory.description: Was fired from Scale AI in 2018 amid a falling out with co-founder Wang; retained roughly 3-5% equity in the company.

trajectory.title: Founded Backend Capital
trajectory.description: Launched Backend Capital, a venture firm, and co-founded HF0, a startup incubator, continuing to build in tech.

trajectory.title: Founded Passes
trajectory.description: Founded Passes, a creator platform competing with OnlyFans and Patreon, leveraging connections with Miami-based entertainment agencies.

trajectory.title: Passes raised $40M Series A
trajectory.description: Passes raised a $40 million Series A and acquired competing creator platform Fanhouse.

trajectory.title: Became youngest self-made female billionaire
trajectory.description: Became the world's youngest self-made female billionaire after Meta's investment in Scale AI valued the company at ~$25 billion, with her stake worth over $1.2 billion.

name: Dylan Field
starting_point: Born in 1992 in Penngrove, California; father was a respiratory therapist, mother a resource specialist teacher; learned algebra at age six; enrolled at Brown University to study computer science in 2009.
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of Figma; net worth estimated at ~$6.6 billion after Figma's IPO in 2025; resides in San Francisco.

trajectory.title: Co-chaired Brown CS group
trajectory.description: Co-chaired Brown University's CS Departmental Undergraduate Group and organized a hackathon with 150 participants while a sophomore.

trajectory.title: Thiel Fellowship and founded Figma
trajectory.description: Received a Thiel Fellowship and dropped out of Brown to co-found Figma with Evan Wallace, moving to San Francisco to build a browser-based design tool.

trajectory.title: Interned at Flipboard
trajectory.description: Interned at Flipboard and LinkedIn while at Brown, gaining early product and engineering experience.

trajectory.title: Figma public launch
trajectory.description: After four years of development, Figma launched publicly as a browser-based collaborative design tool, pioneering real-time multi-player design.

trajectory.title: Adobe acquisition announced
trajectory.description: Adobe announced it would acquire Figma for $20 billion, one of the largest software acquisitions ever.

trajectory.title: Adobe deal scrapped
trajectory.description: The Adobe acquisition was abandoned in December 2023 due to regulatory antitrust concerns in the UK and EU.

trajectory.title: Figma IPO
trajectory.description: Figma went public on the NYSE in July 2025, with shares more than tripling on the first day, valuing the company at nearly $20 billion and making Field a billionaire.

name: Evan Wallace
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Figma and built its browser graphics foundation
starting_point: Studied computer science at Brown University where he met Dylan Field as his teaching assistant; co-founded Figma with Field in 2012.
current_position: Co-founder of Figma; departed from the company in 2023; net worth estimated in the billions following Figma's IPO.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Figma
trajectory.description: Co-founded Figma with Dylan Field after receiving a Thiel Fellowship, moving to San Francisco to build a browser-based vector graphics editor.

trajectory.title: Built browser graphics engine
trajectory.description: Led the technical development of Figma's browser-based graphics rendering engine using WebGL, solving a key engineering challenge.

trajectory.title: Figma public launch
trajectory.description: Figma launched publicly after four years of development, with Wallace's graphics foundation enabling real-time collaborative design in the browser.

trajectory.title: Adobe acquisition announced
trajectory.description: Adobe announced it would acquire Figma for $20 billion, valuing Wallace's stake at billions of dollars.

trajectory.title: Left Figma
trajectory.description: Departed Figma after the Adobe acquisition was scrapped, ending his formal role at the company he co-founded.

trajectory.title: Figma IPO
trajectory.description: Figma went public on the NYSE, with shares tripling on the first day and valuing the company at nearly $20 billion.

name: Whitney Wolfe Herd
starting_point: Born on July 1, 1989 in Salt Lake City, Utah; attended Southern Methodist University where she majored in international studies; grew up in a family affected by difficult relationships.
current_position: Executive chair and CEO (returned March 2025) of Bumble Inc.; net worth estimated at ~$1 billion; resides in Austin, Texas.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Tinder
trajectory.description: Joined Sean Rad's startup at Hatch Labs and became a co-founder of Tinder, naming the app and serving as VP of Marketing, driving campus growth.

trajectory.title: Left Tinder and sued
trajectory.description: Resigned from Tinder in April 2014 and filed a sexual harassment lawsuit; received over $1 million in settlement.

trajectory.title: Founded Bumble
trajectory.description: Founded Bumble with backing from Russian billionaire Andrey Andreev, launching the dating app where women make the first move.

trajectory.title: Bumble rapid growth
trajectory.description: Bumble grew rapidly, reaching millions of users and expanding internationally as a female-first dating platform.

trajectory.title: Andreev sold stake
trajectory.description: Andrey Andreev sold his majority stake in Bumble's parent company after a Forbes investigation into Badoo's culture; Wolfe Herd gained more control.

trajectory.title: Bumble IPO
trajectory.description: Bumble went public in February 2021, making Wolfe Herd the youngest woman to take a US company public and a self-made billionaire.

trajectory.title: Stepped down as CEO
trajectory.description: Stepped down as CEO of Bumble in early 2024, becoming executive chair while Lidiane Jones took over as CEO.

trajectory.title: Returned as CEO
trajectory.description: Returned as CEO of Bumble in March 2025 after Lidiane Jones departed, resuming leadership of the company she founded.

name: Melanie Perkins
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Canva after building Fusion Books
starting_point: Born in 1987 in Perth, Western Australia; mother was a teacher, father a Malaysian engineer of Filipino and Sri Lankan heritage; trained seriously in figure skating and started a small business selling handmade scarves in high school.
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of Canva, valued at ~$42 billion as of 2025; resides in Australia; pledged majority of stake to charitable causes.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Fusion Books
trajectory.description: Co-founded Fusion Books with Cliff Obrecht, a web-based yearbook publisher that let schools create yearbooks using drag-and-drop tools; left university at 19 to pursue it.

trajectory.title: Pitching Canva vision
trajectory.description: Began pitching a broader design platform to investors, meeting Bill Tai in Perth and learning kitesurfing to connect with kiteboarding VCs; faced over 100 rejections.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Canva
trajectory.description: Co-founded Canva with Cliff Obrecht and Cameron Adams, a former Google designer who joined as the third co-founder.

trajectory.title: Canva launched publicly
trajectory.description: Canva launched in August 2013, offering a simple drag-and-drop design platform that quickly gained traction.

trajectory.title: Canva reached unicorn status
trajectory.description: Canva was valued at over $1 billion, making Perkins one of the youngest female tech founders to reach unicorn status.

trajectory.title: Canva valued at $40 billion
trajectory.description: Canva raised funding at a $40 billion valuation, making it one of the most valuable private software companies in the world.

trajectory.title: 185 million monthly users
trajectory.description: Canva surpassed 185 million monthly users and was valued at $42 billion by private investors, with revenue exceeding $4 billion.

name: Ben Francis
starting_point: Born on June 4, 1992 in the West Midlands, England; grew up in Bromsgrove, Worcestershire; attended South Bromsgrove High School; first business was selling car number plates online; worked as a Pizza Hut delivery driver while at university.
current_position: Co-founder, CEO and majority owner of Gymshark; net worth estimated at ~$1.3 billion; appointed MBE in 2023; resides in Solihull, England.

trajectory.title: Built fitness apps
trajectory.description: Developed two fitness apps, Fat Loss Abs Guide and iPhysique, while a student at Aston University, earning around £8,000 from one.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Gymshark
trajectory.description: Launched Gymshark in his parents' garage with school friend Lewis Morgan, initially selling fitness supplements via dropshipping.

trajectory.title: Pivoted to apparel
trajectory.description: Pivoted from supplements to fitness apparel, buying a sewing machine and screen printer; gave free products to fitness YouTubers at a bodybuilding expo, sparking viral growth.

trajectory.title: Stepped down as CEO
trajectory.description: Stepped down as CEO, handing the role to former Reebok director Steve Hewitt, recognizing he lacked executive experience.

trajectory.title: Rotated through leadership roles
trajectory.description: Served as CTO, CMO, and chief product officer over four years to learn different areas of the business.

trajectory.title: Sold 21% stake to General Atlantic
trajectory.description: Sold a 21% stake to General Atlantic for a deal valuing Gymshark at $1.45 billion; retained 70% ownership.

trajectory.title: Returned as CEO
trajectory.description: Returned as CEO of Gymshark, reclaiming the leadership role after six years of learning the business.

trajectory.title: Appointed MBE
trajectory.description: Appointed Member of the Order of the British Empire (MBE) in the 2023 New Year Honours for services to the business sector.

name: Sophia Amoruso
milestone_by_age_26: Built Nasty Gal from an eBay store
starting_point: Born on April 20, 1984 in San Diego, California; of Greek, Italian, and Portuguese American descent; dropped out of school due to depression and ADHD; lived a nomadic lifestyle, hitchhiking and dumpster diving on the West Coast before settling in San Francisco.
current_position: Founder and managing partner of Trust Fund, a venture capital firm investing in pre-seed and seed-stage startups; resides in Los Angeles.

trajectory.title: Started Nasty Gal on eBay
trajectory.description: Started an eBay store called Nasty Gal Vintage while working as a security guard at the Academy of Art University in San Francisco, selling vintage clothing from an '87 Volvo.

trajectory.title: Moved Nasty Gal off eBay
trajectory.description: Moved Nasty Gal from eBay to an independent e-commerce site, building it into a standalone fashion retailer.

trajectory.title: Nasty Gal hit $100M revenue
trajectory.description: Nasty Gal reported over $100 million in revenue, raised $49 million from Index Ventures, and was named one of the fastest-growing companies by Inc. Magazine.

trajectory.title: Published #GIRLBOSS
trajectory.description: Published the New York Times bestselling memoir '#Girlboss,' which was later adapted into a Netflix series in 2017.

trajectory.title: Stepped down as Nasty Gal CEO
trajectory.description: Stepped down as CEO of Nasty Gal in January 2015, distancing herself to focus on her media platform.

trajectory.title: Nasty Gal filed for bankruptcy
trajectory.description: Nasty Gal filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in November 2016; assets were acquired by Boohoo.com for $20 million in February 2017.

trajectory.title: Founded Girlboss Media
trajectory.description: Founded Girlboss Media, creating content for millennial women entrepreneurs, with a podcast network, newsletter, and conferences.

trajectory.title: Founded Trust Fund VC
trajectory.description: Founded Trust Fund, a venture capital firm investing in pre-seed and seed-stage startups, with investors including Marc Andreessen and Chris Dixon.

name: Ritesh Agarwal
milestone_by_age_26: Built OYO's predecessor and joined the Thiel Fellowship
starting_point: Born on November 16, 1993 in Bissam Cuttack, Odisha, India; grew up in a modest Marwari family in Titilagarh; family operated a small shop; began coding at age eight; moved to Delhi in 2011 for college but dropped out.
current_position: Founder and CEO of OYO/PRISM, a hospitality chain operating in 80+ countries; India's youngest billionaire with net worth of ~$2 billion; panellist on Shark Tank India season 3.

trajectory.title: Founded Oravel Stays
trajectory.description: Founded Oravel Stays, an Airbnb-equivalent for the Indian market, at age 18 after moving to Delhi for college.

trajectory.title: Venture Nursery acceleration
trajectory.description: Oravel Stays was accelerated through the Venture Nursery program in Mumbai.

trajectory.title: Thiel Fellowship and launched OYO Rooms
trajectory.description: Won the 2013 Thiel Fellowship receiving $100,000; launched OYO Rooms in May 2013, pivoting from a listing platform to a standardized budget hotel chain.

trajectory.title: Expanded OYO to China
trajectory.description: Launched OYO in China, expanding rapidly into international markets beyond India.

trajectory.title: Raised $1 billion
trajectory.description: OYO raised $1 billion in funding by September 2018, with investors including SoftBank.

trajectory.title: $2 billion share buyback
trajectory.description: Purchased $2 billion in OYO shares, tripling his stake and valuing the company at $10 billion.

trajectory.title: Shark Tank India and IPO plans
trajectory.description: Became the youngest 'Shark' on Shark Tank India season 3; PRISM (OYO's parent) filed for a ₹6,650 crore IPO.

name: Bhavish Aggarwal
starting_point: Born on August 28, 1985 in Ludhiana, Punjab, India; parents were doctors; completed B.Tech in computer engineering at IIT Bombay in 2008; worked at Microsoft Research India for two years.
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of Ola Consumer, founder and CEO of Ola Electric, and founder of Ola Krutrim; net worth estimated at ~$2 billion; resides in Bangalore, India.

trajectory.title: Joined Microsoft Research
trajectory.description: Started career at Microsoft Research India as a research intern, later becoming an assistant researcher; filed two patents and published three papers.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Ola Cabs
trajectory.description: Co-founded Ola Cabs with Ankit Bhati in Bangalore after a bad experience with a taxi; launched the ride-hailing platform in January 2011.

trajectory.title: Ola became unicorn
trajectory.description: Ola Cabs became a unicorn valued at over $1 billion, competing with Uber in the Indian market.

trajectory.title: Founded Ola Electric
trajectory.description: Founded Ola Electric, an EV and battery manufacturing venture, as a separate entity within the Ola group.

trajectory.title: Launched Ola Electric scooters
trajectory.description: Ola Electric launched its first electric scooters from a factory on the outskirts of Bangalore, planned to be run entirely by women.

trajectory.title: Ola Electric IPO and Krutrim unicorn
trajectory.description: Ola Electric went public in August 2024; Krutrim, his AI startup founded in 2023, became India's first AI unicorn valued at $1 billion.

name: Sachin Bansal
starting_point: Born on August 5, 1981 in Chandigarh, India; father was a businessman, mother a homemaker; graduated from IIT Delhi with a B.Tech in Computer Science; worked at Amazon as a senior software engineer before starting Flipkart.
current_position: Managing director of Navi Group, a financial services company; net worth estimated at ~$1.2 billion; resides in Bangalore, India.

trajectory.title: Graduated from IIT Delhi
trajectory.description: Graduated from IIT Delhi with a B.Tech in Computer Science after securing All India rank of 49th on his second IIT JEE attempt.

trajectory.title: Joined Amazon
trajectory.description: Joined Amazon Web Services as a senior software engineer in Bangalore, where he met future co-founder Binny Bansal.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Flipkart
trajectory.description: Co-founded Flipkart with Binny Bansal (not related) as an online bookstore with ₹4 lakh initial capital, operating from an apartment in Koramangala, Bangalore.

trajectory.title: Flipkart expanded categories
trajectory.description: Flipkart expanded beyond books into electronics, fashion, and other categories, becoming India's leading e-commerce platform.

trajectory.title: Stepped down as Flipkart CEO
trajectory.description: Transitioned from CEO to executive chairman of Flipkart, handing day-to-day operations to Binny Bansal.

trajectory.title: Walmart acquired Flipkart
trajectory.description: Walmart acquired a 77% stake in Flipkart for $16 billion; Bansal sold his 5.5% stake for ~$1 billion and exited the company.

trajectory.title: Founded Navi Group
trajectory.description: Founded Navi Group, a financial services company offering digital loans, insurance, and investment products.

name: Nikhil Kamath
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Zerodha after years of trading
starting_point: Born on September 5, 1986 in Shimoga, Karnataka, India; father was a bank executive at Canara Bank, mother ran an event management company; dropped out of school after 10th grade; worked at a call centre earning ₹8,000/month while trading stocks on the side.
current_position: Co-founder of Zerodha and True Beacon; net worth estimated at ~$3.3 billion as of 2025; resides in Bangalore, India.

trajectory.title: Started call centre job and trading
trajectory.description: Dropped out of school and began working at a call centre while studying stock markets during night shifts, earning ₹8,000 per month.

trajectory.title: Started Kamath & Associates
trajectory.description: Became a sub-broker and started a brokerage firm with his brother Nithin to manage high-net-worth individual portfolios.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Zerodha
trajectory.description: Co-founded Zerodha with his brother Nithin, introducing a discount brokerage model that eliminated percentage-based commissions in India.

trajectory.title: Zerodha rapid growth
trajectory.description: Zerodha grew rapidly as India's stock market participation increased, becoming the country's largest retail broker by volume.

trajectory.title: Co-founded True Beacon
trajectory.description: Co-founded True Beacon, an asset management company focused on ultra-high-net-worth investors.

trajectory.title: India's youngest self-made billionaire
trajectory.description: Named one of India's youngest self-made billionaires with a net worth exceeding $2.5 billion, built entirely without external funding.

name: Marques Brownlee
starting_point: Born on December 3, 1993 in Maplewood, New Jersey; attended Columbia High School; joined YouTube in 2008 and started uploading tech review videos in January 2009 as a high school sophomore; attended Stevens Institute of Technology.
current_position: YouTube tech reviewer with 20+ million subscribers across channels; named 'Creator of the Decade' at the 2018 Shorty Awards; professional ultimate frisbee player; resides in New Jersey.

trajectory.title: Uploaded first YouTube videos
trajectory.description: Started uploading screencast tech review videos to YouTube in January 2009 while a high school sophomore, reviewing products he already owned.

trajectory.title: Reached 100,000 subscribers
trajectory.description: Crossed 100,000 subscribers on his MKBHD channel, earning the YouTube Silver Creator Award; featured on Engadget.

trajectory.title: Praised by Google's Vic Gundotra
trajectory.description: Google SVP Vic Gundotra called Brownlee 'the best technology reviewer on the planet right now' in 2013.

trajectory.title: Reached 1 million subscribers
trajectory.description: Crossed 1 million subscribers on YouTube, earning the Gold Creator Award and establishing MKBHD as a major tech channel.

trajectory.title: Graduated from Stevens Institute
trajectory.description: Graduated from Stevens Institute of Technology with a BS degree while continuing to grow his YouTube channel.

trajectory.title: Named Creator of the Decade
trajectory.description: Named 'Creator of the Decade' at the 10th Shorty Awards, cementing his status as the most influential tech reviewer on YouTube.

trajectory.title: 20 million subscribers
trajectory.description: Surpassed 20 million subscribers across his YouTube channels with billions of total video views, interviewing figures like Elon Musk and Tim Cook.

name: PV Sindhu
starting_point: Born on July 5, 1995 in Hyderabad, India to P.V. Ramana and P. Vijaya, both from Andhra Pradesh; started playing badminton at age eight, inspired by Pullela Gopichand and training at his academy.
current_position: Indian badminton player; two-time Olympic medalist (silver 2016, bronze 2020); 2019 BWF World Champion; ranked among Forbes' highest-paid female athletes; resides in Hyderabad.

trajectory.title: Entered international circuit
trajectory.description: Entered the international badminton circuit at age 14, winning bronze at the Sub-Junior Asian Badminton Championships in Colombo.

trajectory.title: Broke into top 20 rankings
trajectory.description: Broke into the top 20 of the BWF World Rankings in September 2012 at age 17; won gold at the Asian Junior Championships.

trajectory.title: First World Championship medal
trajectory.description: Became India's first medallist in women's singles at the BWF World Championships, winning bronze; also won the Malaysian Open Grand Prix gold.

trajectory.title: Olympic silver medal
trajectory.description: Won silver at the 2016 Rio Olympics, becoming the first Indian badminton player to reach an Olympic final; awarded the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna.

trajectory.title: World No. 2 ranking
trajectory.description: Rose to a career-high world ranking of No. 2 in April 2017, establishing herself among the world's elite.

trajectory.title: World Champion
trajectory.description: Became the first Indian to win gold at the BWF World Championships, defeating Nozomi Okuhara in the final.

trajectory.title: Olympic bronze medal
trajectory.description: Won bronze at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics (held in 2021), becoming the first Indian woman to win two Olympic medals.
